entries.title: Linux Detection Engineering - Local Privilege Escalation
entries.description: Seven of the thirteen Linux privilege escalation CVEs we tracked in 2026 turned out to be the same copy-on-write bug pointed at different kernel interfaces. We ran the public proof-of-concept for eleven exploits and two misconfigurations, and noted which rules fired.

entries.title: PuzzleMask: Abusing Plain Prose as a Covert AI Attack Vector
entries.description: During the past two years, LLM use has proliferated to a profound degree. LLMs are sorting job applications, troubleshooting technical issues and researching what sofa will fit your aunt’s living room — all of which require processing mountains of untrusted input. Unfortunately, while LLMs have prodigious talent and breadth of knowledge in some areas, they natively lack one bedrock aspect of human tenacity: the ability to take one look at the shape of an interaction and say “nope, I’m out.” Atta

entries.title: The Shared Clipboard Inside the Sandbox: Cross-Account Data Leakage in ChatGPT
entries.description: Over the past several years, AI assistants have moved far beyond text generation. Modern systems can execute code, install additional dependencies, analyze user files, and access data through connected services. These capabilities significantly increase the practical value of LLMs, but they also change the security model: protecting user data now depends both on the behavior of the model itself and on its execution environment, the tools available to it, and the platform’s internal services.

entries.title: 7th September – Threat Intelligence Report
entries.description: For the latest discoveries in cyber research for the week of 7th Setpember, please download our Threat Intelligence Bulletin.

entries.title: Angry Birds: Toy Ghouls’ new toys
entries.description: Kaspersky GERT experts have discovered new backdoors used by the Toy Ghouls group. One version of the backdoor uses the HiveMQ MQTT broker as its command-and-control server; the other uses the Matrix-based Element messenger.

entries.title: Data access: the hidden cost of security vendor lock-in
entries.description: Getting data into a security platform is always easy; getting it back out is where vendors add cost, extra tooling, and latency, and it is the part of the evaluation most teams overlook.

entries.title: How to correlate Kubernetes audit logs with container runtime data
entries.description: Two fields join the Kubernetes API to what ran inside the pod, and one turns up a container escape your process events never recorded.

entries.title: Gaming the system: how a Chinese-speaking actor turned Brazilian government sites into an SEO weapon
entries.description: Since mid-2025, Check Point Research has tracked a sustained campaign against Brazilian organizations. The tradecraft points to a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group connected to Earth Berberoka, an actor first documented targeting gambling sites across Asia.

entries.title: REVSTEALER ramps up: analysis of up-and-coming infostealer
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs deep dives into REVSTEALER, an emerging infostealer targeting browsers, wallets, and gaming accounts.

entries.title: Linux Detection Engineering - Fileless Execution
entries.description: We reproduced five Linux fileless execution patterns with FENIX, including memfd_create staging, interpreter one-liners, deleted binaries, and in-memory kernel module loads, then mapped each to the Elastic Defend rules that catch it.

entries.title: Mirage Kitten targeting aviation and FinTech sectors across the Middle East and Africa with a new malware set
entries.description: Kaspersky researchers have discovered new Mirage Kitten attacks using previously undocumented malware families: NodeRabbit in Node.js and PollCat in JavaScript.
